original_question: Let X be a separable ordered Banach space such that every order-bounded increasing sequence in X has a supremum. Is that already enough to conclude that every order-bounded increasing sequence in X is norm convergent, without assuming separately that the cone X+ is normal?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 3.2(2): whether the normality assumption on X+ in Theorem 3.1 is redundant.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly keeps the scope to separable ordered Banach spaces, uses the hypothesis that every increasing order-bounded sequence has a supremum, and asks exactly whether one can conclude norm convergence of every such sequence without separately assuming that the cone X+ is normal. That matches the paper’s official question in Open Problem 3.2(2), rather than the broader neighboring question in Open Problem 3.2(1).
missing_details: To be fully self-contained in the paper’s sense, X should be specified as a real ordered Banach space, i.e. a real Banach space equipped with a closed cone X+ inducing the partial order.
The paper’s separability hypothesis is separability in the norm topology.

For an increasing sequence, the paper phrases the hypothesis as being order bounded from above; this is the precise form used in Theorem 2.1 and equivalent here to saying the increasing sequence is order bounded.
The supremum should be stated to exist in X for every such increasing sequence.
The desired conclusion is best named explicitly as the Levi property, i.e. that every increasing sequence in X that is order bounded from above converges in norm.

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be identified as the redundancy of the normality assumption in Theorem 3.1, not as the broader question whether the supremum hypothesis alone forces normality in arbitrary ordered Banach spaces.
refined_question: Let X be a real separable ordered Banach space, ordered by a closed cone X+ that induces the partial order on X. Assume that every increasing sequence in X which is order bounded from above has a supremum in X. Must X have the Levi property; that is, must every increasing sequence in X which is order bounded from above converge in norm? Equivalently, is the assumption that X+ be normal in Theorem 3.1 redundant?
equivalent_formulation: Under the same hypotheses, must X satisfy the equivalent assertions of Theorem 2.1; in particular, must every increasing net in X that is order bounded from above be norm convergent?
justification: In the arXiv version of the paper, the statement your draft is aiming at is formulated explicitly as Open Problem 3.2(2), not as a conjecture in Section 1. Theorem 3.1 proves exactly your desired implication under the additional hypothesis that X+ is normal, and immediately afterward the author asks whether that normality assumption is redundant. Theorem 2.1 supplies the exact name and equivalent reformulations of the conclusion, calling it the Levi property and showing that if this conclusion holds then X+ is automatically normal. So the sharp, paper-faithful standalone version is the redundancy question for Theorem 3.1.
